definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Fearlessness, named with fear among the states (bhāva) of beings that arise from the Lord alone (10.4).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Practice, repeated effort: the yoga of practice is offered to one who cannot hold the thought (citta) steadily on the Lord (12.9); one incapable even of practice is told to be intent on work for him (12.10); in the ranking of 12.12 knowledge is better than practice.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The yoga of practice by which one is to seek to reach the Lord when the thought (citta) cannot be fixed steadily on him (12.9).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Unthinkable: one of the attributes of the imperishable (akṣara) worshipped by those who worship the unmanifest (12.3).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Concerning the self: the knowledge concerning the self (adhyātma-vidyā) is the Lord among the sciences (10.32); Arjuna calls the teaching he has received 'the supreme secret called adhyātma', through which his delusion is gone (11.1).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The sense of 'I': the devotee dear to the Lord is without it (nirahaṅkāra), as also without 'mine' (nirmama) (12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Non-harming, listed among the states of beings that arise from the Lord alone (10.5).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Unborn: the Lord is to be known as unborn and without beginning, the great lord of the world; whoever knows him so is undeluded and freed from all sins (10.3); Arjuna calls him unborn (10.12).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Ignorance, from which darkness is born; out of compassion the Lord, abiding in his devotees' own being, destroys it with the shining lamp of knowledge (10.11).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The imperishable: Arjuna names the Lord 'the imperishable, the supreme to be known' (11.18) and 'the imperishable — being and non-being and what is beyond' (11.37); in ch. 12 'the imperishable, the unmanifest' is the object of a worship distinct from devotion to the Lord, described as indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable and constant (12.1, 12.3). In 10.25 and 10.33 akṣara means 'syllable, letter'.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Nectar: Arjuna is never sated hearing the Lord's words, his 'nectar' (10.18); the horse Uccaiḥśravas is 'born of the nectar' (10.27); the teaching on the dear devotee is 'this nectar of dharma' (dharmyāmṛta, 12.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Portion: whatever is glorious or mighty has arisen from a portion of the Lord's splendour (tejas) (10.41); he stands supporting this whole world with a single portion (10.42).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Undivided devotion (bhakti ananyā), by which alone the Lord can in the form shown be known, seen and entered in truth (11.54) — not by the Vedas, austerity, giving or sacrifice (11.53); cf. worship with 'undivided yoga' (ananya yoga) (12.6).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Non-being: Arjuna addresses the Lord as the imperishable, 'being and non-being (sad asat), and what is beyond' (11.37).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The self: 'I am the self seated in the resting-place (āśaya) of all beings' (10.20). In ch. 10–12 the word is also often simply reflexive — the Lord knows himself by himself (10.15); 'show yourself' (11.4); 'by my own yoga' (11.47); 'self-restrained' (12.11, 12.14) — and in 11.24 antarātman is Arjuna's own inner being.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The unmanifest: the imperishable worshipped by the second group in Arjuna's question (12.1, 12.3); the hardship of those whose awareness (cetas) is attached to the unmanifest is greater, for the unmanifest goal is reached with difficulty by the embodied (12.5).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Devotee: one who does the Lord's work, holds him supreme, is unattached and without enmity toward any being comes to him (11.55); the devotee dear to him bears the marks of 12.13–19; those who with faith attend to this 'nectar of dharma' are exceedingly dear (12.20).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Devotion: the wise, knowing the Lord as the origin of all, worship (bhajante) him (10.8); to those ever yoked who worship him with love he gives the yoga of understanding (10.10); by undivided devotion alone he can be known, seen and entered in truth (11.54).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: State, being: understanding, knowledge, forbearance, pleasure and pain, fear and fearlessness and the rest are the various states (bhāva) of beings arising from the Lord alone (10.4–5); Arjuna asks in which bhāvas the Lord is to be contemplated (10.17); the wise worship him 'endowed with bhāva' (10.8).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Seed: the Lord is whatever is the seed of all beings; nothing moving or unmoving could exist without him (10.39).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna calls Kṛṣṇa 'the supreme brahman (paraṃ brahma), the supreme abode, the supreme purifier' (10.12).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Understanding: first among the states of beings that come from the Lord (10.4); the worshippers of the imperishable are even in understanding everywhere (samabuddhi, 12.4); 'let your understanding enter into me' (12.8); the dear devotee has manas and buddhi offered to the Lord (12.14). Named distinctly from manas, citta and cetas.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The yoga of understanding which the Lord gives to those ever yoked who worship him with love, and by which they come to him (10.10).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of beings I am cetanā' (10.22): the sentience or awareness of living beings, named beside manas as chief of the faculties.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Awareness (cetas): the hardship is greater for those whose cetas is attached to the unmanifest (12.5); the Lord soon delivers from the ocean of death and saṃsāra those whose cetas is set on him (12.7); seeing the gentle form again, Arjuna is 'sacetāḥ', with his cetas restored (11.51). Named distinctly from manas, buddhi and citta.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Thought (citta): the devotees have their citta on the Lord (maccittāḥ, 10.9); if one cannot hold the citta steadily fixed on him, the yoga of practice is prescribed (12.9).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Restraint, among the states of beings that arise from the Lord (10.4).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Giving: a state of beings that arises from the Lord (10.5); not by gifts can he be seen in the form Arjuna saw (11.48, 11.53).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Sight of the Lord: even the gods ever long for a sight (darśana) of the form Arjuna has seen (11.52).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The gods do not know the Lord's origin, for he is their beginning (10.2, 10.14); they are seen within the universal form (11.15) and long for a sight of it (11.52).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna calls the Lord 'the unchanging guardian of the eternal dharma' (11.18); the teaching of the dear devotee's marks is 'this nectar of dharma' (dharmyāmṛta, 12.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Steadfastness: one of the seven feminine excellences that are the Lord (10.34); before the fierce form Arjuna finds no dhṛti (11.24).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Meditation: those who, laying down all actions in the Lord, worship him meditating (dhyāyantaḥ) with undivided yoga, he soon delivers (12.6–7); in the ranking of 12.12 meditation is superior to knowledge, and relinquishing the fruit of actions is superior to meditation.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The divine eye the Lord gives Arjuna, since he cannot see the Lord's sovereign form with his own eye (11.8).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Pain, paired with pleasure among the states from the Lord (10.4); the dear devotee is the same in pain and pleasure (12.13, 12.18); the unmanifest goal is reached 'with pain', i.e., with difficulty (duḥkham, 12.5).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The gāyatrī metre: 'of metres I am the gāyatrī' (10.35).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Secret: of secret things the Lord is silence (10.38); Arjuna calls the teaching he has received 'the supreme secret called adhyātma' (11.1).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna calls the Lord the world's object of worship and its 'weightiest teacher' (guru garīyān) (11.43).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Faculty / sense: of the indriyas the Lord is manas (10.22); the worshippers of the imperishable restrain the whole group of the senses (indriya-grāma) (12.4).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord: to be known as 'the great lord of the world' (lokamaheśvara) (10.3); addressed as supreme lord (parameśvara, 11.3), lord of all (viśveśvara, 11.16), lord of gods (deveśa, 11.25) and 'the lord to be praised' (11.44).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Muttered recitation, counted as a sacrifice: 'of sacrifices I am the japa-yajña' (10.25).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The sacrifice of muttered recitation, named as the Lord among sacrifices (10.25).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Knowledge: a state of beings that comes from the Lord (10.4); the Lord is 'the knowledge of the knowers' (10.38); his 'lamp of knowledge' destroys the darkness born of ignorance (10.11); in 12.12 knowledge is better than practice, and meditation superior to it.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Time: 'of those that reckon I am time' (10.30); 'I alone am imperishable time' (10.33); answering 'who are you?', the Lord says 'I am Time, grown mighty, the destroyer of worlds' (11.32); his mouths are 'like the fire of time' (kālānala, 11.25).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Action: those who lay down all actions in the Lord (12.6); doing actions for his sake leads to perfection (12.10); the fruit of all actions is to be given up (12.11–12).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Compassionate (karuṇa): a mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.13).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Hardship, toil: 'greater is the kleśa of those whose awareness (cetas) is attached to the unmanifest' (12.5) — used here in its general sense, not as the Yoga system's technical 'afflictions'.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Forbearance: a state from the Lord (10.4), one of the seven feminine excellences that are the Lord (10.34), and, as kṣamin, a mark of the devotee dear to him (12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Unchanging: an attribute of the imperishable worshipped as the unmanifest (12.3).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Greatness: Arjuna has heard in detail of the Lord's imperishable greatness (11.2).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Friendliness: the devotee dear to the Lord is friendly (maitra) and compassionate (12.13).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Mind: of the faculties the Lord is manas (10.22); Arjuna's manas is shaken with fear (11.45), and he is told to look again with a glad manas (11.49); the most yoked worship the Lord fixing their manas on him (12.2); 'place your manas on me alone' (12.8); the dear devotee has manas and buddhi offered to him (12.14). Named distinctly from buddhi, citta and cetas.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Manus, who with the seven great seers were born from the Lord's mind and from whom come the creatures of the world (10.6).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Silence: of secret things the Lord is silence (10.38); the dear devotee is silent (maunin) (12.19).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Retentive intelligence, one of the seven feminine excellences that are the Lord (10.34).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Delusion: whoever knows the Lord as unborn and beginningless is undeluded (asaṃmūḍha) (10.3); Arjuna says his delusion is gone through the teaching (11.1); the Lord tells him not to be bewildered (vimūḍhabhāva) by the terrible form (11.49).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Death: 'I am all-seizing death' (10.34); the Lord delivers his devotees from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Instrument, occasion: 'by me alone have these already been slain; be merely the instrument (nimitta-mātra)' (11.33).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Without 'mine': a mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of utterances I am the one syllable (ekam akṣaram)' (10.25) — a syllable the Gītā names as oṃ at 8.13.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Supreme lord: Arjuna's address as he asks to see the Lord's sovereign form (11.3).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Life-breath: the devotees' prāṇas have 'gone into' the Lord (madgataprāṇāḥ) (10.9).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Grace, favour: Arjuna repeatedly asks the Lord to be gracious (prasīda, 11.25, 11.31, 11.45) and seeks his grace (prasādaye, 11.44); the Lord, gracious (prasanna), showed him the supreme form (11.47).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Person: Arjuna calls the Lord the eternal divine Person (10.12), the everlasting Person (11.18) and the ancient Person (11.38).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Highest Person: Arjuna's address to the Lord (10.15, 11.3).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Seer: the great seers do not know the Lord's origin, for he is their beginning (10.2); the seven great seers were born from his mind (10.6); all the seers proclaim him supreme (10.13).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Form: Arjuna asks to see the Lord's sovereign form (rūpam aiśvaram) (11.3); the Lord shows his forms by hundreds and thousands (11.5), then again his own gentle, human form (11.50–51).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Calm: a state from the Lord (10.4); before the fierce form Arjuna finds no śama (11.24).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Laying down: those who lay down (saṃnyasya) all actions in the Lord and worship him (12.6).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The ocean of death and saṃsāra, from which the Lord soon delivers those whose awareness (cetas) is set on him (12.7).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Peace, which follows immediately on relinquishing the fruit of actions (12.12).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Contentment: the dear devotee is ever content (santuṣṭa, 12.14) and content with whatever comes (12.19).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Being: Arjuna addresses the Lord as the imperishable, 'being and non-being (sad asat), and what is beyond' (11.37).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'I am the sattva of those who have it' (10.36) — goodness or strength; in 10.41 sattva means simply 'a being'.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Truthfulness, among the states of beings that arise from the Lord (10.4).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Purity: the dear devotee is pure (śuci) (12.16).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Perfection, accomplishment of the goal, attained even by doing actions for the Lord's sake (12.10).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Memory, one of the seven feminine excellences that are the Lord (10.34).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Faith: those who worship the Lord endowed with supreme faith are the most yoked (12.2); those who with faith attend to this nectar of dharma are exceedingly dear to him (12.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Pleasure, paired with pain among the states from the Lord (10.4); the dear devotee is the same in both (12.13, 12.18).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Austerity: a state of beings that arises from the Lord (10.5); not by fierce austerities can he be seen in the form Arjuna saw (11.48, 11.53).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Splendour: the Lord is the splendour of the splendid (10.36); whatever is glorious arises from a portion of his tejas (10.41); the universal form is a mass of tejas (11.17), made of tejas (11.47), heating the universe with its tejas (11.19, 11.30).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Contentment, among the states of beings that arise from the Lord (10.5).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Relinquishment: giving up the fruit of all actions, prescribed for one unable even to work for the Lord (12.11); ranked above meditation, with peace following immediately (12.12).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Impartial, 'seated apart': a mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.16).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Worship (upa-√ās, pari-upa-√ās): Arjuna contrasts those who worship the Lord with those who worship the imperishable unmanifest (12.1); the Lord describes both kinds (12.2–6); the devotees 'attend to' this nectar of dharma (12.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Speech, one of the seven feminine excellences that are the Lord (10.34).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Discussion: 'of those who debate (pravadatām) I am vāda' (10.32).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Of the Vedas the Lord is the Sāmaveda (10.22); not by the Vedas can he be seen in the form Arjuna saw (11.48, 11.53).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Manifestation: the Lord's own divine manifestations, by which he stands pervading the worlds (10.16), told by their chief instances since there is no end to them (10.19, 10.40); whoever knows his vibhūti and yoga in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7); whatever being is endowed with vibhūti has arisen from a portion of his splendour (10.41).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Whose form is all': Arjuna's address to the Lord seen with endless form, without end, middle or beginning (11.16).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Sacrifice: of sacrifices the Lord is the japa-yajña (10.25); not by sacrifices can he be seen in the form Arjuna saw (11.48, 11.53).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord's own yoga, to be known together with his vibhūti (10.7, 10.18); his sovereign yoga (yogam aiśvaram), seen with the divine eye (11.8); by his own yoga (ātmayoga) he showed the supreme form (11.47). Of the practitioner: 'unwavering yoga' (10.7), 'undivided yoga' (12.6), 'the yoga of practice' (12.9).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Lord of yoga: Arjuna's address when asking to be shown the Lord's imperishable self (11.4); Sañjaya calls Hari 'the great lord of yoga' (11.9).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Yoked: those ever yoked who worship the Lord with love (10.10); Arjuna asks about the devotees ever yoked (12.1); those who fix the mind on him are 'the most yoked' (yuktatama) (12.2).
